main_text.p: tam in hoc quam in illo objecto. Suppono solem omnes flores in horto æqualiter luce & calore suo imbuere, hic flos vegetat aliis arefcentibus, num recte dicerem floris vegetanti? o tu reliquis beatior, plus debes soli, quam reliqui. Sic enim subinnuerem, solem reliquos flores luce & calore non illustrare, hunc vero tantum beare, quod patet esse falsum.

R. I. Suarez ait: non expedit de suis gloriari. Suar. in 9 pufc de au- xil.l 3.c 20. Valentia, gloriari (inquit) potest (converfus) Valent. tom. 2. d.8. q.3, p.4. non in Domino solo, sed tum in Domino, tum deinde in se. Fonseca ait, posse homines in se gloriari, sed tutius esse (ut dicunt Chrysostomus & Ambrosius) non gloriari ob periculum superbiæ & inanis gloriæ. fig. 14. Fonsec. lib. 6 metaph. Arminiani collat. hag. p. 333. Negant omnem gloriationem esse malam. Corvinus contr. Tilen. c. 5. p. 136. c 2. q.5. sect. 9. hominem tam se fe-parare dici posse, quam ait scriptura, hominem se sanctificare, purgare, vivificare, salvare. Rcsp 1. An homines in Domino gloriari possint, insanit qui in quæstionem aut ad partes vocet, ut ait scriptura, 1.Cor. 1. 30. & 31. Sed quæritur an liceat gloriari in eo quod recepimus, quasi non recepissemus. Ex adversariorum vero doctrina converfus, gratia præveniente, ut o&o [?], instructus, ficut & instruitur non converfus, potest gloriari in actu libero suæ converfionis activæ, quam a Deo non magis habet, quam non-converfus. 2. page.notes: Running head "GRATIÆ." is set in spaced capitals. Page number read as 441 from a worn "44¹" at the top right; the final digit is doubtful. "ut o&o" is unclear and may be "ut octo"; marked [?]. Marginal references at the right are very small and partly cut; their line breaks and exact positions are approximate. Greek and Latin reference numbers as printed. The catchword "cum" and signature "Ee 5" are at the foot. Hyphenated line-end words ("fi-cut", "gloria-ri", "fe-parare", "non-converfus", "ve-lint") were joined, with the printed hyphen kept only where the word is a compound ("non-converfus").
